name: Cave 1 — Padmapani Murals
problem: Described as 'oldest cave in the complex' but Cave 1 dates to late 5th century CE; Caves 9 and 10 are older (2nd century BCE).
evidence: Wikipedia + multiple sources confirm Caves 9 and 10 (2nd century BCE) predate Cave 1 (late 5th century CE). See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ajanta_Caves
suggested_fix: Change 'The oldest cave' to 'An important cave' or 'A later Vakataka-period cave featuring'

name: Durga Temple
problem: Described as '5th-century temple' but the Durga Temple is dated to 7th-8th century CE (not 5th century). May be confusing with the broader Aihole site which has 5th-century temples like Lad Khan.
evidence: Multiple sources including Wikipedia and Hubpages confirm Durga Temple was built 7th-8th century (reign of Vikramaditya II, 733-746 CE). See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durga_temple,_Aihole and https://discover.hubpages.com/education/Durga-temple-of-Aihole-Karnataka-7th-cent-Vesara-style-of-Architecture
suggested_fix: Change '5th-century temple' to '7th-8th century temple' or '7th-century temple'

name: St Mary's Island
problem: Hexagonal basalt columns stated as '40 feet high' but tallest confirmed columns are approximately 6 metres (20 feet), not 40 feet.
evidence: Wikipedia and Outlook Traveller confirm the tallest columns are about 6 m (20 ft). See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Mary's_Islands and https://www.outlooktraveller.com/experiences/nature/explore-the-lesser-known-st-marys-island-of-udupi-in-karnataka
suggested_fix: Change '40 feet high' to '20 feet high' or '6 metres high'

name: Sindhudurg Fort
problem: Described as '16th-century' fort but Sindhudurg Fort was built 1664-1667 (17th century), not 16th century. Also distance (500m offshore vs 1.5 km), bastions (22 vs 42-52), and wall height (40 feet vs ~30 feet/9-10m) are inaccurate.
evidence: Multiple sources confirm construction 1664-1667 under Shivaji. See https://reismagosfortgoa.com/ (Reis Magos comparison), https://www.re-thinkingthefuture.com/case-studies/a2791-sindhudurg-fort-the-1664-architecture-marvel-constructed-on-an-island, Maharashtra Tourism https://maharashtratourism.gov.in/fort/sindhudurg/
suggested_fix: Change '16th-century island sea fortress built by Shivaji' to '17th-century island sea fortress built by Shivaji (1664-1667)'. Update distance to ~1.5 km, bastions to 42, walls to ~30 feet.

name: Borra Caves Main Chamber
problem: Stated as '150-metre-deep limestone cave system, India's deepest' but actual depth is 80 metres (260 feet), not 150 metres.
evidence: Wikipedia and Outlook Traveller confirm caves extend to 80 m depth, not 150 m. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borra_Caves and https://www.outlooktraveller.com/experiences/adventure/borra-caves-in-andhra-pradesh-are-the-deepest-limestone-caves-in-india
suggested_fix: Change '150-metre-deep' to '80-metre-deep' or '260-foot-deep'

name: Cave 26 — Reclining Buddha
problem: Described as 'One of two chaityas' but Ajanta Caves has 5 chaityas total (caves 9, 10, 19, 26, 29), not two.
evidence: Multiple sources confirm 5 chaityas at Ajanta: caves 9, 10, 19, 26, 29. Cave 26 is one of five. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ajanta_Caves
suggested_fix: Change 'One of two chaityas' to 'One of five chaityas' or simply remove the quantifier and say 'A major chaityagriha'

name: Vembanad Lake
problem: Lake length is stated as 68km, but verified sources confirm it is 96.5 km long.
evidence: Wikipedia (Vembanad) and Kottayam District Government website state the lake is 96.5 km long, the longest lake in India. The 68km figure may refer only to a section between Thanneermukkom and Alappuzha.
suggested_fix: Change '68km long' to '96.5 km long (or approximately 60-68 km in the Kumarakom/Alleppey section)' to reflect the full lake while acknowledging regional segments.

name: Mandrem Beach
problem: Beach is described as a '3 km stretch', but verified sources indicate 790 metres to 1.5 km.
evidence: Multiple sources (Thrillophilia, Tripadvisor, local guides) confirm Mandrem Beach stretches 790 meters to 1.5 kilometres. The longer 9.44 km measurement refers to the broader Arambol-to-Chapora coastal stretch, not Mandrem Beach itself.
suggested_fix: Change '3 km stretch' to '1.5 km stretch' or 'approximately 1-2 km of uncrowded sand' to match verified measurements.

name: Ibrahim Roza
problem: Description claims the mausoleum 'is believed to have inspired the Taj Mahal's design', but this claim is unproven and contested.
evidence: Search results show the claim appears in tourism marketing (Tripadvisor reviews, some blogs), but Wikipedia and architectural sources note the influence is unproven. One source suggests the reverse—that Malik may have been inspired BY the Taj Mahal, given the Taj (1653) was completed well after Ibrahim Roza (1627).
suggested_fix: Change to 'believed by some to have influenced subsequent Mughal architecture' or remove the inspiration claim entirely and focus on its own architectural merits: '...with intricate calligraphy and serene gardens, showcasing Adil Shahi architecture at its finest.'

name: Hiranyakeshi Temple
problem: Described as part of Ashtavinayak circuit, but Hiranyakeshi is a Shiva temple dedicated to Goddess Parvati, not a Ganesha temple. The 8 Ashtavinayak temples are at Ojhar, Morgaon, Theur, Ranjangaon, Siddhatek, Lenyadri, Mahad, and Pali—none include Amboli.
evidence: Ashtavinayak temples list verified via Wikipedia and official Kerala tourism sources. Hiranyakeshi Temple is a 12th-century Shiva shrine to Parvati, not part of any Ganesha pilgrimage circuit.
suggested_fix: Remove 'part of the Ashtavinayak circuit pilgrimage route' clause. Update to 'Ancient Shiva temple dedicated to Goddess Parvati (Hiranyakeshi) with a self-manifested Shivling called Hiranyakeshwar.'

name: Sawantwadi Palace
problem: Sawantwadi Palace is located in Sawantwadi town, not Amboli. While accessible via Amboli Road (~12km away), it is a distinct destination. The POI entry incorrectly attributes it to Amboli.
evidence: Official Sindhudurg tourism website and multiple sources confirm the palace is in Sawantwadi, address: NH 17, Khaskilwada, Sawantwadi, Sindhudurg District, Maharashtra 416510. Amboli is a separate destination ~12km away.
suggested_fix: Remove from Amboli POIs entirely. Create a Sawantwadi destination entry with this palace. Alternatively, note in description: 'Historic palace in nearby Sawantwadi town (12km away), accessible via Amboli Road.'

name: Bahubali Monolith
problem: Description states the monolith was 'installed on Ratnagiri Hill in 1973,' but it was sculpted in 1973 and positioned (installed) in February 1982.
evidence: Official Shri Kshetra Dharmasthala website confirms: 'sculpted in 1973 by sculptor Renjala Gopalkrishna Shenoy' and 'positioned atop the Ratnagiri Hill in February 1982 by Dr. D. Veerendra Heggade.'
suggested_fix: Change 'installed on Ratnagiri Hill in 1973' to 'sculpted in 1973 and installed on Ratnagiri Hill in 1982' or simply 'A 39-foot monolith of Lord Bahubali installed in 1982.'

name: Car Museum
problem: Museum founder name is given as 'Manjunatha Dharma Veerendra Heggade,' which is malformed. The correct name is 'D. Veerendra Heggade.' The title 'Manjunatha Dharma' conflates the temple's name (Manjunatha) with the museum's name (Manjusha).
evidence: Multiple sources including The Week and official Dharmasthala tourism confirm the founder is 'D. Veerendra Heggade,' the hereditary administrator of the Dharmasthala temple trust. No such compound name 'Manjunatha Dharma Veerendra Heggade' exists.
suggested_fix: Change 'Manjunatha Dharma Veerendra Heggade' to 'D. Veerendra Heggade' (or 'Dr. D. Veerendra Heggade').

name: Theyyam Ritual Performance
problem: Description states 'Performances occur December–May during harvest season,' but Theyyam season actually runs November–May, with peak season in November-December. The season should begin in November, not December.
evidence: Multiple sources including DTPC Kannur and Kerala Tourism confirm the Theyyam season is November–May, with November and December being the peak months. Onam (July/August) is one harvest festival with Theyyam, but the main season is Nov–May.
suggested_fix: Change 'December–May' to 'November–May' or 'Peak season November–May.'

name: Cave 1 (Shiva Cave)
problem: Description incorrectly dates Cave 1 to '1st-2nd century BCE' when it was actually excavated around 550 CE during the Early Chalukya period (~500-year error).
evidence: Badami cave temples were carved 550-750 CE under Early Chalukya patronage. Cave 1 specifically dates to approximately 550 CE under Pulakeshin I (543-566 CE). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badami_cave_temples
suggested_fix: Change '1st-2nd century BCE' to '6th century CE' or '550 CE (Chalukya period)' to align with Early Chalukya dating

name: Arthur's Seat
problem: Named after Sir Arthur Mallet, not Arthur Stanley
evidence: Arthur's Seat Mahabaleshwar sources consistently identify it as named after Sir Arthur Mallet, a British officer. Multiple sources (gomahabaleshwar.com, travelsetu.com) confirm this spelling and attribution.
suggested_fix: Change 'Named after British administrator Arthur Stanley' to 'Named after British officer Sir Arthur Mallet'

name: Gopalaswamy Betta Viewpoint
problem: Distance claim of '32km inside Bandipur National Park' unverified; authoritative sources cite 19km from Bandipur or 9km from Hangla
evidence: Wikipedia and multiple tourism sources (thrillophilia.com, travelsetu.com) indicate 19 km from Bandipur town; 9 km from Hangla; some sources note 25-30 km range. No source supports 32 km.
suggested_fix: Change '32km inside Bandipur National Park' to '19km from Bandipur' or 'at the core of Bandipur National Park'

name: Cabo de Rama Fort
problem: Listed as '16th-century Portuguese fort' but main fortifications date to 1763, not 16th century
evidence: Search results (tripoto.com, traveltriangle.com) clarify: Fort origins predate Portuguese; Chapel of Saint Anthony built 1591 (16th c.), but major Portuguese fortifications added in 1763 after capture
suggested_fix: Change '16th-century Portuguese fort' to 'Historic fort with 16th-century Portuguese chapel and major fortifications added in 1763'

name: Minicoy Lighthouse
problem: Description states '300-foot tall' but actual height is 49.5 meters (162 feet), not 300 feet.
evidence: Wikipedia and official sources confirm 49.5m (162 ft) height. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minicoy_Island_Lighthouse
suggested_fix: Replace '300-foot tall' with '49.5 meters high' or '162 feet tall'

name: Chennakesava Temple
problem: Description states 'UNESCO World Heritage Site (2024)' but UNESCO recognition occurred in 2023, not 2024.
evidence: UNESCO designation as Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas in 2023. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennakeshava_Temple,_Belur
suggested_fix: Change '(2024)' to '(2023)' in the description

name: Fort Geldria
problem: Description claims Fort Geldria was 'the first European settlement in India', but Portuguese arrived in India in 1498 (Vasco da Gama) and captured Goa in 1510, over 100 years before Fort Geldria (1613).
evidence: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama first reached India in Calicut on 20 May 1498 and established trading posts. Goa was captured by the Portuguese in 1510. Fort Geldria was built by the Dutch in 1613, making it the first Dutch settlement, not the first European settlement. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasco_da_Gama and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Geldria
suggested_fix: Change '...the first European settlement in India' to '...the first Dutch settlement in India' or '...the Dutch Republic's first settlement in India'

name: Dhyana Buddha Statue
problem: Description claims the statue is a '125-foot bronze Buddha statue', but the statue is made of reinforced concrete, not bronze.
evidence: The Dhyana Buddha statue is made of reinforced concrete and covered with sandstone panels, completed in 2015. Multiple sources confirm it is concrete/stone, not bronze. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhyana_Buddha_statue
suggested_fix: Change '125-foot bronze Buddha statue' to '125-foot concrete Buddha statue' or '125-foot stone and concrete Buddha statue'

name: Coracle Rides
problem: Description claims coracles are a '2000-year craft' at Hogenakkal, implying the boats themselves have that pedigree. Actual coracles used today are modern reconstructions of an ancient boat design.
evidence: Coracle rides at Hogenakkal use modern reconstructions of this ancient design. While coracles as a design concept have ancient origins (dating back 2000+ years in various cultures), the specific boats at Hogenakkal are contemporary vessels. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coracle
suggested_fix: Change '2000-year craft' to 'ancient boat design' or 'traditional round boats inspired by ancient design'

name: Sula Vineyards
problem: Description states 'established in 2000' but Sula Vineyards was founded in 1999 by Rajeev Samant. The first commercial wine release occurred in 2000 after the 1999 inaugural harvest.
evidence: Sula Vineyards was founded in 1999 with the first bottle of wine sold in 2000 (inaugural harvest 1999). Source: https://sulavineyards.com/our-history.php and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sula_Vineyards
suggested_fix: Change 'established in 2000' to 'established in 1999' or 'first wine released in 2000'

name: Colonial Port Warehouses Remnants
problem: Description contains misspelling: 'Godalpur was a prominent trading port' should be 'Gopalpur'. The correct spelling throughout historical records is 'Gopalpur' (Gopalpur-on-Sea), not 'Godalpur'.
evidence: All historical sources and the government of Odisha refer to this location as 'Gopalpur' or 'Gopalpur-on-Sea'. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gopalpur,_Odisha and https://apps.odishatourism.gov.in/
suggested_fix: Change 'Godalpur' to 'Gopalpur' in the description

name: Cape Comorin Beach
problem: Description claims 'Only place with sunrise and sunset both over sea' which is geographically false—many coastal peninsulas allow both views.
evidence: Kanyakumari actually allows viewing sunrise over Bay of Bengal and sunset over Arabian Sea (different seas). This is a common tourist myth. Multiple sources confirm the phenomena occurs at other locations. Source: https://www.incredibleindia.gov.in/en/tamil-nadu/kanniyakumari
suggested_fix: Replace with: 'India's southernmost tip where Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea, and Indian Ocean converge. Unique for viewing sunrise over Bay of Bengal and sunset over Arabian Sea from the same location.'

name: Dutch Church (Munroe Island)
problem: Description states church was 'built by the Dutch in 1878' but it was actually built by the Portuguese in 1518, with major renovations in 1878 adopting Dutch architectural elements.
evidence: Wikipedia and official sources confirm Portuguese construction in 1518, not Dutch in 1878. 1878 was renovation date. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Church,_Munroe_Island
suggested_fix: Replace with: 'Red brick church originally built by the Portuguese in 1518, later renovated in 1878 with Dutch architectural elements. Showcases blend of Dutch and traditional Keralan architectural styles.'

name: Murud Janjira Fort
problem: Described as '15th-century offshore fort built under Malik Amber's rule', but the stone fort was built in 1567 AD (16th century) by Malik Ambar, replacing an earlier 15th-century wooden structure.
evidence: Wikipedia Murud-Janjira: 'After its construction in 1567 AD' and 'Itbarrao Koli...built this island in the 15th century' (wooden fort); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murud-Janjira
suggested_fix: Change to '16th-century offshore stone fort, rebuilt in 1567 AD by Malik Ambar from an earlier 15th-century wooden garrison'

name: Borra Caves
problem: Described as 'Second largest cave system in the Indian subcontinent, 3,229m long total.' But Borra is NOT the second largest (Belum Caves is), and Wikipedia states Borra's length is ~200m, not 3,229m.
evidence: Wikipedia Borra Caves: 'length is about 200 m (660 ft)'; search reveals Belum Caves (3,200+ metres) is second largest after Krem Liat Prah; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borra_Caves
suggested_fix: Remove second-largest ranking and 3,229m length. Replace with accurate description: 'Limestone cave system with stalactite and stalagmite formations, approximately 200m in explored length. One of India's deepest caves (80m depth).'

name: Dr Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary
problem: Description understates sanctuary area (400 hectares vs actual 178 ha) and bird species (200+ vs actual 473+).
evidence: Wikipedia + multiple tourism sources confirm sanctuary is 178 hectares and hosts 473+ bird species. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salim_Ali_Bird_Sanctuary
suggested_fix: Update to: 'Mangrove sanctuary on Chorao Island covering 178 hectares. Home to 473+ bird species including kingfishers, egrets, osprey, and painted storks.'

name: Barehipani Falls
problem: Waterfall height stated as 217m but actual height is 399m total (with 259m single drop). Error is ~45% understatement.
evidence: Wikipedia + multiple sources confirm Barehipani is 399m total height and second-highest waterfall in India. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barehipani_Falls
suggested_fix: Update description to: 'India's second-highest waterfall at 399-metre height (259m single drop), located in northern Simlipal.'

name: Joranda Falls
problem: Height stated as 181m but most authoritative sources cite 150m.
evidence: Wikipedia and multiple sources consistently report 150m height, though some sources do cite 181m. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joranda_Falls
suggested_fix: Update to: 'Waterfall in southwestern Simlipal with 150-metre height.'

name: Elephanta Cave Temple
problem: Entry fee listed as ₹600 but this is only for foreign nationals; Indian visitors pay ₹40. Description does not clarify.
evidence: Official sources confirm ₹40 for Indian/SAARC visitors, ₹600 for other foreign nationals. See https://traveltriangle.com/maharashtra-tourism/mumbai/places-to-visit/elephanta-caves/
suggested_fix: Update entry_fee to clarify: '₹40 (Indian/SAARC), ₹600 (foreign)' or just '₹40-600' with description noting foreigner rate.

name: Kanakeshwar Temple
problem: Temple construction date listed as 1764 but should be 1674.
evidence: Per TourMyIndia and Grokipedia sources: 'The unique architecture of the temple was built in 1674 and is the finest example of Hoysala style of architecture'. https://www.tourmyindia.com/states/maharashtra/kanakeshwar-devasthan-temple-alibaug.html
suggested_fix: Change '1764' to '1674' in description.

name: Athirapally Falls
problem: Description claims 'India's largest by monsoon volume' but this is factually incorrect. Chitrakote Falls (Indravati River) is India's largest waterfall by monsoon volume with ~300m width. Athirapally is the largest in Kerala only.
evidence: Wikipedia List of waterfalls in India by height; multiple sources confirm Chitrakote Falls as 'India's largest waterfall by volume of water discharge' and 'The Niagara of India'. Athirapally is verified only as 'largest in Kerala'. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jog_Falls; https://padhai.ai/blogs-padhai/list-of-top-waterfalls-in-india
suggested_fix: Remove 'India's largest by monsoon volume' and replace with 'Largest waterfall in Kerala' or 'one of Kerala's largest waterfalls by volume'.

name: Athirapally Falls
problem: Height listed as '80-foot' but verified height is 81.5 feet (approximately 24-25 meters).
evidence: Wikipedia Athirappilly Falls and multiple Kerala tourism sources confirm height as 81.5 feet. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athirappilly_Falls
suggested_fix: Update height from '80-foot' to '81.5-foot' or round to '82-foot'.

name: Kodaikanal Lake
problem: Stated area of 60 sq km is more than double the actual size of Kodaikanal Lake.
evidence: Kodaikanal Lake is approximately 24-25 sq km, consistently documented across tourism sources and official data. The 60 sq km figure represents a significant factual overestimation.
suggested_fix: Change '60 sq km' to '24 sq km' or '~24-25 sq km' in the description

name: Mahad Ashtavinayak
problem: Temple dedication is listed as 'Vighneshwara' but Mahad's Ashtavinayak is actually dedicated to 'Varadvinayak'. Vighneshwara is located at Ozar (7th in sequence).
evidence: Official Ashtavinayak sequence: 1.Mayureshwar 2.Siddhivinayak 3.Ballaleshwar 4.Varadvinayak (Mahad) 5.Chintamani 6.Girijatmaj 7.Vighneshwara (Ozar) 8.Mahaganapati. Source: https://www.ashtavinayak.in/mahad-varadvinayak-ganpati-ashtavinayak.php
suggested_fix: Change dedication from 'Vighneshwara' to 'Varadvinayak (the wish-fulfilling Ganesha)'

name: Pali Ashtavinayak
problem: Temple at Pali is listed as 'Third Ashtavinayak temple dedicated to Girijatmaja' but Pali actually hosts Ballaleshwar (3rd in sequence). Girijatmaj is the 6th Ashtavinayak, located at Lenyadri, not Pali.
evidence: Official Ashtavinayak sequence: Pali = Ballaleshwar (3rd). Girijatmaj = Lenyadri (6th, carved into cave 8 with 307 steps). Source: https://www.shreeballaleshwarpali.org/ and https://www.ashtavinayak.in/lenyadri-girijatmaj-ganpati-ashtavinayak.php
suggested_fix: Change 'Girijatmaja' to 'Ballaleshwar (the wish-granting Ganesha)', noting that Pali is the 3rd in sequence

name: Srirangapatna Fort Walls
problem: Description states '16th-century fort' but historical sources indicate the fort was fortified in the 15th century, with later Tipu Sultan renovations in the 18th century.
evidence: Fort fortification began 15th century; Tipu Sultan renovated and strengthened the fort in 18th century. British breached walls in 1799. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seringapatam and https://www.britannica.com/place/Srirangapatna
suggested_fix: Change '16th-century fort' to '15th-century fort (renovated by Tipu Sultan in the 18th century)'

name: Arjuna's Penance
problem: Dimensions stated as 27m high × 90m wide; actual documented dimensions are 29m × 13m (96 ft × 43 ft).
evidence: Wikipedia and official sources confirm 96 by 43 feet (29 m × 13 m). See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Descent_of_the_Ganges_(Mahabalipuram) and https://www.tamilnadutourism.tn.gov.in/destinations/arjunas-penance
suggested_fix: Change description to: 'World's largest bas-relief, 29m high × 13m wide (96 ft × 43 ft). 7th–8th century Pallava carved tableau depicting Hindu mythology scenes.'

name: Manginapudi Beach
problem: Claims 'Manginapudi Lighthouse (1611)' but lighthouse was first established in 1852, with the one at Manginapudi specifically built in 1858.
evidence: Wikipedia Machilipatnam Lighthouse states: 'The first light at Machilipatnam was commissioned in 1852 at a different location' and 'first established in 1858, at Manginapudi Beach.' See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machilipatnam_lighthouse and https://www.dgll.nic.in/DGLL-light-house-location/about-vishakhapatnam/machilipatnam-lighthouse
suggested_fix: Change description to: '11km stretch of sandy beach on the Bay of Bengal with year-round calm waters. Offers swimming, jet skiing, speed boating, and fishing community walks. Machilipatnam Lighthouse (1858) stands nearby.'

name: Nandankanan Zoological Park
problem: Description states 'first Indian zoo in WAZA' but Nandankanan was established in 1960 and only joined WAZA in 2009, not at founding.
evidence: Wikipedia + verified sources confirm: 'It became the first zoo in India to join World Association of Zoos and Aquariums (WAZA) in 2009', not 1960. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandankanan_Zoological_Park
suggested_fix: Change 'first Indian zoo in WAZA' to 'joined WAZA in 2009' or drop the WAZA claim entirely and keep only 'established in 1960'

name: Kailasa Temple (Cave 16)
problem: Description claims 'took over 100 years to complete' but documented evidence shows construction took only 18-20 years.
evidence: Wikipedia and verified sources state: 'it only took 18 years to finish' and 'it only took 18 years to complete the construction using iron chisels and hammers only', though scholars note it would take 100+ years with modern machinery. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kailasa_Temple,_Ellora
suggested_fix: Remove 'took over 100 years to complete'. Replace with accurate statement: 'completed in approximately 18-20 years during the 8th century' or note the comparison to modern machinery separately

name: Kanakakkunnu Palace Gardens
problem: Palace is attributed to destination 'trivandrum' but Kanakakkunnu Palace is actually located in Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum) as part of that city, making this entry duplicative with Kuthiramalika Palace in the same destination. However, the destination_id is correct—the actual issue is Palace exists in Thiruvananthapuram and is ~800m NE of Napier Museum (which is also listed separately). This is not a separate destination POI.
evidence: Multiple sources (Wikipedia, Kerala Tourism, official Incredible India) confirm: 'Kanakakkunnu Palace is situated in Thiruvananthapuram' and located near Napier Museum. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanakakkunnu_Palace
suggested_fix: Verify with founder: this palace is in Trivandrum city proper, not a distinct destination. If the POI is valid, confirm it as a separate attraction in Trivandrum (alongside other Trivandrum palaces). Entry appears correct as-is if these are meant to be multiple palace attractions in Trivandrum.

name: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple
problem: Description claims 'Over 3,000 years old' but documented evidence places temple at 2,300+ years minimum, with scholarly debate and no conclusive proof exceeding 3,000 years.
evidence: Wikipedia and verified scholarly sources state: 'The earliest recorded mention of the temple is from the 8th or 9th century CE, although the temple is likely older' and 'the history of the Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple can be traced back to at least 300 BCE' (~2,300 years), with speculative claims of 5,000+ years but 'it is not possible to determine with any exactitude' the true founding date. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padmanabhaswamy_Temple
suggested_fix: Change 'Over 3,000 years old' to 'at least 2,300 years old (dating to 300 BCE)' or 'one of India's oldest temples with origins likely before 300 BCE' to stay within documented evidence

name: Chamundi Hill
problem: Description states 'Climb 1000 steps' but the actual number is 1,008 steps (the main recognized official count), or 1,180 steps total including alternate routes.
evidence: Multiple verified sources including FKT (Fastest Known Time) confirm: 'Chamundi 1008 Steps' is the official main pathway. Some sources cite 1,001 or 1,180 total steps including secondary routes. https://fastestknowntime.com/route/chamundi-1008-steps-india
suggested_fix: Change 'Climb 1000 steps' to 'Climb 1,008 steps to reach the pristine temple' (the official count) or '1,008+ steps' to be precise
